newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends up 8 cts despite weak oil products.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends up 8 cts despite weak oil products.

text.p: IPE Brent ended slightly higher on Wednesday after a late rally and despite downward pressure from oil products.
June Brent ended up eight cents a barrel at $18.07 after climbing near the close from the days low of $17.81.
"All the products were weak and leaning on Brent a bit, not just the gas oil," said a trader.
Gasoline and heavy fuel were both soft with poor end user demand strong selling on swaps.
Gas oil ended 75 cents a tonne lower at $163 for May a few hours earlier on the IPE.
Brokers MeesPierson Derivatives pegged next support on June Brent at $17.80 and others saw further support at $17.65, the nine-month low hit earlier this month.
Despite steady demand from refiners Brent was under pressure from CFDs swaps and inter-month spreads which both slipped lower over the day.
Refinery profit margins in Europe have faltered in recent days although at over $2 a barrel for Brent they remain bouyant compared to recent months.
Dealers expect demand to recover soon in Europe if gasoline and gas oil manage to stay avoid further sharp losses.
They said news of a resumption of oil loading at Nigeria's Bonny terminal had little market impact.
Other bearish news included a big cut in demand from Romania over the next few months.
An oil industry official said that country would cut imports to 400,000 tonnes per month in the summer from 750,000 tonnes in April.
Prices had firmed earlier after the release of weekly data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which traders construed as being mildly bullish. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 4984
